title: Micro-mentorship sync — compact notes (Sasha Huang)
agenda_items: 1) Quick wins since last sync (5 min)
2) Career checkpoint: signals & stretch goal alignment (10 min)
3) Blockers: technical debt + oncall heatmap (10 min)
4) Sprint scope: prioritization ask for platform infra (8 min)
5) Mentorship action: lead a postmortem & runbook onboarding (7 min)
content:
Context: Short, focused 1:1 with direct report (Eden Park). Goal is to surface traction, unblock quickly, and set one mentorship stretch for the next 4 weeks. Keep this micro-format to make follow-ups frictionless.

Notes taken during prep: 
- Recent signals: p99 inference latency for benchmarking job dropped 8% after kernel tweak; cost per token on staging reduced ~6% with batching change. Need metric owners to confirm numbers (Ravi to validate).
- Career signal: Eden is interested in stepping into small cross-team initiative ownership (infra->dev-ex). Wants to run a short experiment to reduce onboarding time for new model teams.
- Technical debt: items piling in model-compat layer — specifically, legacy code path in quantize_helper that inflates memory by 12% on long sequences. Eden flagged it as medium priority.
- Oncall note: Eden handled two incidents last sprint; one required rollback of PR #482. Need to update rollback checklist and postmortem template to account for quantization regressions.

Open questions to ask Eden: 
- How confident are you about shipping the lightweight onboarding experiment in two sprints? What signal would make you delay?
- Which parts of the quantize_helper refactor do you want pairing help on vs owning solo?
- Do you feel the oncall runbook covers quantization/rollbacks specifically? If not, what would you add?

Coaching prompts (use if conversation stalls): 
- "Tell me about a recent decision you made that surprised you — what did you learn?"
- "If you had one constraint removed for a week, what would you choose to accelerate progress?"

Risks to surface: 
- If refactor waits, risk of repeated rollbacks during high-load experiments (customer-facing).
- Taking on cross-team onboarding could slow current deliverables if not scoped tightly.

Draft suggestions for Eden: 
- Scope onboarding experiment to a single model family and a 1-week synchronous test cohort. Measure new-hire time-to-first-success and doc completeness.
- Break quantize_helper refactor into: (a) small tests + benchmarks, (b) interface stabilization, (c) incremental rollout behind feature flag. Aim to merge (a) in 2 weeks.

Action items (compact format):
- Eden — write 1-page experiment plan for onboarding trial; include success criteria and measurement (due 2026-11-17).
- Sasha — schedule 30m cross-team kickoff with DevEx and Solutions Eng (target 2026-11-12).
- Ravi — validate p99 latency and cost numbers from staging (due 2026-11-09).
- Eden + Sasha — pair on unit tests for quantize_helper, focus on edge-case sequences (prep session 2026-11-13).
- Sasha — draft rollback checklist addition for quantization regressions and attach to oncall runbook (due 2026-11-20).

Follow-ups to track next 1:1: 
- Experiment plan submitted and feedback status.
- Test coverage and benchmark results for quantize_helper.
- Incident blameless review summary (if applicable).

Quick personal note to self: Keep this micro-format so Eden can iterate quickly; avoid turning into a full PRD in this 1:1. Celebrate the oncall wins — explicitly call out the solid incident handling in the meeting.

Short closing line to paste into the 1:1 invite: 
"Micro-sync: 30m to review recent wins, unblock quantization work, and agree on a small cross-team onboarding experiment. Bring any quick metrics or drafts you want feedback on."
